The root cause is in `XmlDeclaration.outerHtmlHead`. When an XML declaration is constructed programmatically via `new XmlDeclaration("xml", baseUri, false)` followed by `attr("version", ...)` / `attr("encoding", ...)` (as `Document.ensureMetaCharsetElement` does when no declaration exists yet), the serializer emits `<?` + `getWholeDeclaration()` + `>`, producing `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8">` — missing the trailing `?` before `>`.
